notes.text:
This is an unverified bounded-calculus reconstruction, not a complete audit or solution of original P16.7. No supplied note, verdict, hash or compilation is used as a mathematical premise. The domain is the actual quotient X=(G_m^2)^an_K/<(t,2),(3,t)>, K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8. Ordinary tropical rectangles of widths less than one give injective quotient charts; the compact fundamental polyannulus covers X and only finitely many closed deck graphs meet bounded chart products. Conventional analytic gluing and descent (Conrad--Temkin Lemmas4.2.3--4.2.4, finite chart covers, not the infinite-sheeted covering) give the compact Hausdorff good smooth separated boundaryless pure-dimensional-two carrier. The packet's nonalgebraization primary chain has not been independently whole-audited here; it is retained separately as DATA. None of the following estimates uses an algebraization.

On charts tau=(-log|z1|,-log|z2|), rho=|tau|^2/2, theta=DD rho. Reference changes are smooth affine unit logarithms. C consists of finite continuous a with rho+a in the ENTIRE minimal continuous CLD psh sheaf. All stages are retained; no global ordinary smooth psh approximation is presumed. Published inputs, at their actual hypotheses, are CLD v2 (25 July2025)8.1.7--8 minimal continuous sheaf;8.2.4 convex nondecreasing composition;8.5.1 continuous multiplication of positive currents under local uniform convergence;8.5.5 positivity/closedness of DD(uT) for continuous psh u and positive closed T;8.7.1--4 recursive products, continuity and symmetry;8.8.4--5 continuous dpsh extension and smooth DD-null changes;7.2.8--12 Radon and coefficient measures on locally differentially separated charts;15.7.1 calibrated tropical calculus on separated pure-dimensional analytic spaces;5.11.1 smooth Stokes/Green with boundary. The boundary is empty here. Smooth cutoffs/approximation/partitions are CLD6.2.4--8 on these paracompact charts. Arbitrary-multiplier closedness8.6.7 is not used. Define theta_a=theta+DDa, B(a,b)=theta_a wedge theta_b and MA(a)=B(a,a). All products are actual positive Radon measures.

The extra all-stage Green argument is as follows. Complete smooth gradients in the positive Hilbert seminorm against any positive closed(1,1) T, locally with nonnegative smooth cutoffs. A uniformly zero smooth sequence with a strong gradient limit pairs to zero with every smooth Hilbert test by closedness, so the limit gradient is zero. Partitions and Leibniz patch the domains; bounded CONTINUOUS coefficients act with the uniform norm bound. For L_Tf=DD(fT) signed Radon, strong/uniform smooth approximation gives Q_T(f,g)=-integral g L_Tf and Q_(T,chi)(f)=one half integral f^2 DDchi wedge T-integral chi f L_Tf. If psh f_j converge uniformly, take nested cutoffs chi,eta, eta=1 near supp chi, and a common bound B on the WHOLE support of eta. For epsilon=||f_j-f_k|| there, positivity gives
Q_(T,chi)(f_j-f_k)<=epsilon^2||DDchi wedge T||_TV/2+2B epsilon||chi||infinity||DDeta wedge T||_TV.
Hence gradients are strongly Cauchy, distributional positivity survives, and the minimal-sheaf argument includes every continuous stage. Differences and finite patching prove symmetric Green Q_T(f,g)=-integral f DD(gT)=-integral g DD(fT), Q_T(f)>=0. Smooth one-variable composition with bounded derivative has its strong chain rule by uniform convergence of derivative multipliers and strong convergence of gradients. No discontinuous multiplier is needed.

Every bounded mixed product has mass two, since exact terms integrate to zero. The reference mass and full reference measure are justified below. Define E(a)=one third integral a[theta^2+B(a,0)+MA(a)]. Cubic expansion and Green give, for a_t=(1-t)a+tb, E'(a_t)=integral(b-a)MA(a_t), E''(a_t)=-2Q_theta_at(b-a). Thus E is concave and monotone, E(0)=0, E(a+c)=E(a)+2c, and
E(b)-E(a)=one third integral(b-a)[MA(a)+B(a,b)+MA(b)].
For a<=b each nonnegative integral on this right is at most3(E(b)-E(a)). The full bounded dual D(mu)=sup_(p in C)(E(p)-integral p mu) forces mass two by constants whenever it is finite. Tangent gives D(MA(q))=E(q)-integral q MA(q). For nonpositive p,q,r with E>=-C, the three nonnegative terms of -3E(q) give D(MA(q))<=2C, hence integral(-p)MA(q)<=3C. Since B(q,r)<=2MA((q+r)/2), integral(-p)B(q,r)<=6C. Green then gives Q_theta_q(p),Q_theta(p)<=6C.

For f=a-b, g=(a+b)/2, h=w-g, put I=integral f(MA(b)-MA(a))=Q_theta_a(f)+Q_theta_b(f)>=0. Product transgression yields Q_theta_w(f)-I/2=Q_theta_a(f,h)-Q_theta_b(f,h). Both sides are -integral f DDf wedge DDh. Since |h|<=-w+(-a-b)/2, its MA moments are<=6C and mixed moments<=12C. Expansion of Q_theta_a(h) bounds it by12C+3C+6C=21C, and the same holds for b. Direct-sum Cauchy--Schwarz proves Q_theta_w(f)<=Psi_C(I), Psi_C(t)=t/2+sqrt(42Ct).

Gauss normalization is actual analytic comparison. GR v2 (17 September2025)Definition4.1 tests every analytic curve after every complete analytic extension; the UNNUMBERED Section1.2 is the CLD-to-classical bridge. Proposition4.2 gives functoriality and decreasing-net closure; Theorem6.4 is affinoid Shilov maximum, not upper regularization. Local uniform classical closure follows by errors<=2^-j and shifts3*2^-j, so all C stages are recognized. Fix the actual z2 Gauss point and work on the actual curve G_m over its completed residue field. Annulus endpoint comparison shows q^2/2+a(Gauss(q,r2)) convex. Period one bounds its subgradients between q-1/2 and q+1/2. Swapping coordinates proves each coordinate Gauss restriction is1/2-Lipschitz. Small coordinate polyannuli and their four Shilov vertices give a(x)<=a(Gauss(tau(x))). Thus sup_Xa=max_Sa; normalized sup0 gives -1/2<=a|_S<=0 on S=R^2/Z^2. Off S a Laurent polynomial has strict cancellation below its monomial maximum. Locally coordinate tropicalization then lies in its finite tropical hypersurface of dimension at most one, and the coordinate(2,2) reference form vanishes. CLD5.10.1--2 and14.5.2--3, identity pleasant moments, saturated degree-one calibration and raw2!, give the actual measure theta^2=2 Lebesgue on S, not merely its mass.

For each finite grid D_N=(N^-1 Z/Z)^2 fix a base vertex o and connect all vertices by finitely many coordinate-radius paths, partitioned into injective boxes. In a horizontal piece CLD18.6.2 gives DD max(0,log(|z2|/r2)) equal to integration over the ACTUAL Gauss fibre G_m_H(eta_r2)(z1). The source is separated boundaryless equidimensional; the coordinate morphism is smooth relative dimension one. A bounded cap w=max(0,delta+epsilon psi-rho0), zero on an outer collar, has theta_w=epsilon times this fibre current inside. Canonical primitive degreeONE calibration and Cauchy--Schwarz on a path of length ell give squared endpoint difference<=ell/epsilon times Q_theta_w(f). Positivity supplies strong curve convergence of ambient approximants, so this holds at ALL continuous stages. Vertical pieces are identical. Sum the finite path constants to obtain A_N and finitely many fixed normalized caps w_l with |f(xi)-f(o)|<=A_N max_l sqrt(Q_theta_w_l(f)). No varying Gauss section is made analytic, and no finite-extension degree is inserted into the fixed residue-field fibre integral.

At every total graded-dimension-two x, support kernel is zero by Abhyankar, and completion adds no initials by smaller-error approximation. Two homogeneous independent Laurent initials give a weighted Gauss image. CLD11.6.5(c), at relative interior with dimensions<=2, reduced target and full image, and11.6.3 give a local finite-flat rankD representative with singleton Gauss fibre. Pleasant calibration14.5.2--3 and the soft-max gradient image simplex of area1/2, with raw2!, give (DD max(0,log(|P1|/r1),log(|P2|/r2)))^2=D delta_x locally. Finite properness and the singleton fibre justify actual upstairs concentration. Global collar caps give w_x in C with MA(w_x)>=alpha_x delta_x, alpha_x>0. The whole test has finite D; no finite dual of a Dirac component is inferred.

The ordered quantitative bound is also reconstructed: for p<=q, nonpositive energies>=-L, d=E(q)-E(p), the positive cocycle gives I(p,q)<=3d. For T=theta_w+theta_p,k=w-p, Green gives integral(q-p)MA(w)<=3d+sqrt(Q_T(q-p)Q_T(k)). The all-test estimate gives Q_T(q-p)<=3I/2+sqrt(42LI); four3L moment bounds give Q_T(k)=I(p,w)<=12L. Hence the integral is<=F_L(d)=3d+sqrt(12L*(9d/2+sqrt(126Ld))). Positivity gives the same point bound divided by alpha at an atom.

The full new bounded arguments are in scoped-paper.tex. notes.detailedSummary: For normalized a,b in C with E>=-C, explicit moduli Omega_C(I),H_C(I)->0 bound integral|a-b|theta^2, integral|a-b|MA(a), integral|a-b|MA(b), and E(max(a,b))-E(a/b), without an ordering hypothesis or common lower sup-norm bound. Fixed bounded-test absolute moments also vanish. A smooth absolute-value ramp paired against signed Radon DD(aT) avoids unproved indicator-gradient rules. notes.text:
This uses only the earlier own bounded reconstruction n1, at the same actual carrier, full continuous CLD sheaf and raw mass two. Let C_C={a in C:sup_Xa=0,E(a)>=-C}, C>=0. For arbitrary a,b in C_C, not assumed ordered, put f=a-b and I=integral f(MA(b)-MA(a)). Let Psi_C(t)=t/2+sqrt(42Ct). For the fixed N-grid caps in n1 put C_N=max(C,max_l[-E(w_l)],0), and define
Omega_C(t)=min(1,inf_(N>=1)[4/N+4A_N sqrt(Psi_C_N(t))]),
H_C(t)=Omega_C(t)+sqrt(6C)[sqrt(t)+sqrt(Psi_C(t))].
Every A_N,C_N is finite and depends only on the fixed grid geometry and C, not on a,b. Both moduli tend to zero: first fix N and let t->0, then let N->infinity. No uniform growth bound for the grid constants is needed.

The theorem is
E((a+b)/2)-(E(a)+E(b))/2=I/8,
integral|f|theta^2<=Omega_C(I),
integral|f|MA(a)<=H_C(I), integral|f|MA(b)<=H_C(I),
0<=E(max(a,b))-E(a)<=H_C(I), and likewise for b.
For fixed bounded nonpositive w, C'=max(C,-E(w),0), also
integral|f|MA(w)<=Omega_C(I)+[sqrt(Q_theta_w(w))+sqrt(Q_theta(w))]sqrt(Psi_C'(I)).
The test may have nonskeletal support. These are actual analytic measure statements; S is used only to fix additive constants.

Proof of the midpoint and reference estimates. Along a_t=(1-t)a+tb the second derivative is -2[(1-t)Q_theta_a(f)+tQ_theta_b(f)]. Twice integrating gives the midpoint deficit (Q_theta_a(f)+Q_theta_b(f))/8=I/8 exactly. Each Gauss restriction is coordinate1/2-Lipschitz, so f|S is coordinate1-Lipschitz. Every S point has circle-l1 distance<=1/N from a grid vertex. The finite-path estimate and all-test estimate of n1 give osc_S f<=2/N+2A_N sqrt(Psi_C_N(I)). Both Gauss functions have maximum zero, so min_S f<=0<=max_S f; thus sup_S|f| is bounded by that oscillation. Multiply by the reference mass two. Also |f|<=1/2 on S, giving integral|f|theta^2<=1. Infimizing proves the Omega bound.

The essential new absolute-value step is entirely bounded. Take F_epsilon(q)=sqrt(q^2+epsilon^2). It converges uniformly to |q|, and its continuous derivative has absolute value<=1. By the strong-chain rule in n1, Q_R(F_epsilon(f))<=Q_R(f) for every positive closed test R needed here. Green pairs F_epsilon(f) with DD(aR), which IS a signed Radon measure. It does not require DD(F_epsilon(f)R) to be Radon, nor a strong limit of indicator derivatives. Since MA(a)-theta^2=DD(a(theta_a+theta)), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
integral F_epsilon(f)MA(a)<=integral F_epsilon(f)theta^2+sqrt(Q_theta_a(f)Q_theta_a(a))+sqrt(Q_theta(f)Q_theta(a)).
Pass uniformly against the finite signed measures to |f|. Now Q_theta_a(f)<=I, Q_theta(f)<=Psi_C(I), and both a-slot energies<=6C. This proves H_C for a; the same argument proves b. Replacing a by fixed w proves the stated fixed-test bound with the fixed finite w energies. Only CONTINUOUS gradient multipliers occur.

For m=max(a,b), monotonicity and the tangent inequality at a give
0<=E(m)-E(a)<=integral(m-a)MA(a)=integral(b-a)_+MA(a)<=H_C(I).
Use b for the other endpoint. m is an actual finite continuous maximum in C, normalized sup0 with energy>=-C; no minimum, rooftop or infinite maximum is assumed psh.

Point consequence. At a full-dimensional x use the fixed atom w_x from n1, normalized by subtracting its supremum, and L_x=max(C,-E(w_x-sup w_x),0). Apply the ordered n1 estimate to a<=m and b<=m. Positivity of the whole atomic test gives
|a(x)-b(x)|<=[F_Lx(E(m)-E(a))+F_Lx(E(m)-E(b))]/alpha_x<=2F_Lx(H_C(I))/alpha_x ->0 as I->0.
This is a separate quantitative estimate at EVERY full-dimensional point. The constants need not be uniform in x. It says nothing about finite full dual of an isolated Dirac measure or values/poles of a hypothetical limit elsewhere.

Variational consequence for any prescribed positive Radon mu of raw mass two with finite FULL D(mu). Define F_mu(a)=E(a)-integral a mu, invariant under constants, and D_C(mu)=sup_(a in C_C)F_mu(a), a finite real number>=0. For a,b let epsilon_a=D_C-F_mu(a), epsilon_b=D_C-F_mu(b). The midpoint h=(a+b)/2 has E>=-C and sup h<=0; h-sup h belongs to C_C and has the same F. Linearity of the measure term therefore gives I/8=F_mu(h)-(F_mu(a)+F_mu(b))/2<=(epsilon_a+epsilon_b)/2, so I<=4(epsilon_a+epsilon_b). Maximizing nets exist by approximation of the real supremum, not assumed attainment. Thus every such net is Cauchy in L1(MA(w)) for EACH fixed bounded w, Cauchy at every full point, and has pairwise finite-maximum energy gains tending to zero. No countable dense set or full-support finite Radon measure is needed.

No actual analytic representative is constructed from this tuple or these L1 limits. In particular this does not prove USC, membership in G, nonordered energy-sublevel compactness or obstacle orthogonality; GR6.5 needs already USC and cannot fill that gap. The new absolute moving moment theorem is NOT asserted for every generatedG endpoint. The full original existence theorem remains open. Complete proofs and all hypotheses appear in scoped-paper.tex and the ENTIRE proof-companion.txt. A new standard-library check verifies the midpoint identity on all four basis monomials of cubic polynomials, which is an exhaustive FINITE algebra identity, not an infinite-dimensional correctness certificate.

notes.detailedSummary: For mu<=sum beta_l MA(w_l), beta_l>0, w_l bounded continuous actual theta-psh, normalized a has F_mu(a)<=-e+B0+B1 sqrt(e), e=-E(a). Thus D(mu)<=B0+B1^2/4 and a maximizing tail has e<=[(B1+sqrt(B1^2+4(B0+1)))/2]^2. notes.text:
This uses earlier own notes n1 and n2. Let mu be any prescribed positive Radon measure with mu(X)=2 and mu<=sum_(l=1..k) beta_l MA(w_l), where beta_l>0 and the w_l are fixed bounded members of the actual entire continuous classC. This is domination of an arbitrary prescribed measure in a delimited special class, not a restriction mu=MA(u), a support restriction to a skeleton or a finite-atomic inverse construction. Normalize each w_l by its finite supremum and put c_l=-E(w_l)>=0. Define
A_l=sqrt(6)[sqrt(Q_theta_w_l(w_l))+sqrt(Q_theta(w_l))],
B0=sum beta_l(1+A_l sqrt(c_l)), B1=sum beta_l A_l.

For arbitrary normalized a in C let e=-E(a)>=0. The actual reference measure and Gauss bound give integral(-a)theta^2<=1. Product transgression and Green give
integral(-a)MA(w_l)=integral(-a)theta^2+Q_theta_w_l(a,w_l)+Q_theta(a,w_l).
The mixed gradient bounds of n1, with energy bound max(e,c_l), and Cauchy--Schwarz give
integral(-a)MA(w_l)<=1+A_l sqrt(max(e,c_l))<=1+A_l sqrt(c_l)+A_l sqrt(e).
As -a>=0, measure domination now implies
integral(-a)mu<=B0+B1 sqrt(e),
F_mu(a)=E(a)-integral a mu<=-e+B0+B1 sqrt(e)<=B0+B1^2/4.
Every competitor can be normalized because the raw mass is exactly two; therefore the FULL bounded dual D(mu) is finite. The zero competitor gives D>=0, and actual maximizing nets exist by the definition of a finite real supremum.

On a maximizing tail F_mu(a)>=-1. Then e-B1 sqrt(e)<=B0+1; solving the quadratic in sqrt(e) gives
e<=C_mu=[(B1+sqrt(B1^2+4(B0+1)))/2]^2.
This is a genuine uniform energy bound, not a presumed variational maximizer or a renaming of the desired equation. For two tail competitors, use the full supremum D(mu) in the midpoint argument: midpoints are full competitors, so I<=4[(D-F_mu(a))+(D-F_mu(b))]. Apply n2 with C=C_mu. Thus every normalized full-dual maximizing net is Cauchy against EACH fixed bounded test MA(w), at EVERY full-dimensional point, and in its pairwise moving endpoint absolute moments and finite-maximum energy gains.

Domination additionally gives integral|a-b|mu<=sum beta_l integral|a-b|MA(w_l)->0. Completeness of L1(mu) supplies a measurable L1 limit; completeness of the real numbers supplies the finite full-point coordinate limits. Finally E(a)=F_mu(a)+integral a mu converges, since both terms converge. These are Cauchy and measurable-limit conclusions, NOT a representative construction. No pointwise values including poles off the full-dimensional set, no USC representative, and no generatedG membership of these limits is proved.

The measure domination is an additional special-class scope and is NOT established for every positive raw-mass-two finite-FULL-dual measure. We do not claim an equation solution even in this special class. Original nonordered analytic representability, envelopes/orthogonality and prescribed-measure existence remain unresolved. The entire proof, including actual bounded input reconstruction, appears in scoped-paper.tex, Theorem labelled coercive, and the ENTIRE proof-companion.txt. There is no new field extension, zero-mass probability normalization or alternative inverse measure operator.
